The Affordable Care Act (ACA), signed in 2010, passed Congress strictly along party lines: the Senate approved it 60–39 (all Democrats and independents in favor, all Republicans opposed) in December 2009, and the House concurred 219–212 (219 Democrats in favor, all 178 Republicans and 34 Democrats opposed) in March 2010.

Federal costs for ACA marketplace subsidies grew steadily from ~$18 billion in 2014 but surged after 2021 due to enhanced premium tax credits introduced in the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) and extended through 2025 by the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). ARPA passed in March 2021 on party lines (House 220–211 with one Democrat opposing, Senate 50–49). The IRA followed in August 2022, also party-line (Senate 51–50 with VP tiebreaker, House 220–207; all Democrats in favor, all Republicans opposed).

These Democratic-led enhancements drove the sharp cost increase to ~$138 billion in 2025, per nonpartisan estimates from CBO, KFF, and CRFB.
